How to estimate a private company's revenue from public signals

Private companies don't publish revenue. Their licenses, filings, job ads, vehicles and permits still show how big they are. This guide shows how to read those signals together and turn them into a range with a confidence level.

To estimate a private company's revenue, collect several independent public signals of its size: headcount from job ads, staff pages and benefit-plan filings, plus licenses, permits, fleet and locations. Multiply headcount by a revenue-per-employee band typical for the industry, check it against a second method such as payroll, and report a range with a confidence level.
To turn signals into dollars, use two methods that rely on different inputs, and let the range cover both.
Run it from the lower of the two low ends to the higher of the two high ends. If the methods don't overlap at all, the headcount or a band is wrong. Find out which before you report anything.
Several independent signals agree, and the two methods give ranges that overlap.
The company, signals and bands are made up to show the method. Real bands vary by region and service mix.

The low end comes from the payroll method and the high end from the headcount method. Four independent signals agree on about 50 people with a fleet to match, the methods overlap, and the one signal that disagrees has a known cause.
